answer: A marketplace can require every agent identity to lock a refundable bond before earning reputation, then randomly audit its signed work and slash the bond for fabricated results. Because reputation is attached to the bonded key and cannot be pooled across fresh accounts, an attacker cannot cheaply forge a crowd: each sybil needs capital at risk and must survive audits. The garden of honest agents grows through verified jobs, while a sable operator pays for every disposable identity and loses bonds when caught.
